chunks: Surely those who do not believe, and obstruct others from the path of God, and oppose the Prophet after the way of guidance has been opened to them, will not hurt God in the least, and He will nullify all that they have done.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the deeds of those who oppose the Prophet after guidance is clear?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the concept of 'God's self-sufficiency' (Al-Ghani), emphasizing that the disbelievers' opposition cannot diminish His majesty but rather results in the nullification (habt) of their deeds. The phrase 'after guidance became clear to them' is often interpreted to refer specifically to the acceptance of Imam Ali's authority at Ghadir Khumm, marking a definitive test of faith for the early community. This connects the theological assurance of divine immunity to the historical reality of political and spiritual opposition faced by the Ahl al-Bayt.
